updateTarget.displayName: Build and Test Your First AWS Lambda Function

programme.displayName: Build and Test Your First AWS Lambda Function
programme.subtitle: Create, test, observe, and manually clean up a first Node.js Lambda function
programme.description: Create a small Node.js 24 AWS Lambda function in Europe (London), test it with harmless JSON input, review its CloudWatch Logs output, and manually remove only the resources created by this Follow Along.
programme.learningOutcome: Create an IAM user without creating credentials, create and deploy your own Node.js Lambda function, invoke it with a fixed test event, inspect its log output, and manually remove the exact practice resources.

phases.title: Prepare a practice identity
phases.description: Create a clearly named IAM user in your own account without creating credentials or permissions in this Follow Along.

phases.title: Create and test your Lambda function
phases.description: Create a Node.js 24 Lambda function in eu-west-2, deploy a small area-calculation handler, and run a fixed JSON test event.

phases.title: Observe and clean up
phases.description: Inspect the invocation evidence in CloudWatch Logs, verify the practice resources, and manually delete only the resources created here.

tasks.title: Create a Practice IAM User
tasks.goal: Create an IAM user named follow-along-lambda-user in your own AWS account without creating a password, access key, or permissions policy.
tasks.whyItMatters: An IAM user is an identity in your AWS account. Creating this clearly named practice user introduces account identities while avoiding credentials and permissions changes that are outside this Lambda exercise.

consoleSteps.title: Open IAM
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The IAM console opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Use your own AWS account. Do not paste credentials, passwords, access keys, or private information into this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Open user creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Specify user details page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Name the practice user
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The user name is follow-along-lambda-user.
consoleSteps.warning: Use this exact fixed name so that the final manual cleanup identifies only the practice user.

consoleSteps.title: Do not create console credentials
consoleSteps.expectedResult: No console password is created for this practice user.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not create a password, access key, or other credential for this user in this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Do not add permissions
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The practice user has no permissions from this Follow Along.
consoleSteps.warning: This Follow Along does not propose, create, or attach any IAM policy. Continue to use your existing authorized account session for the Lambda tasks.

consoleSteps.title: Create the practice user
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Users list includes follow-along-lambda-user.

cliSteps.explanation: Use this as the CLI alternative to the console creation path, not after creating the same user in the console.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies the new IAM user named follow-along-lambda-user.
cliSteps.warning: IAM is global, so this command does not use --region. Do not create credentials or attach permissions as part of this Follow Along.

verification.title: Confirm the practice user exists
verification.instruction: In IAM Users, search for follow-along-lambda-user.

tasks.title: Create and Deploy Your Lambda Function
tasks.feature: Lambda function and default execution role
tasks.goal: Create follow-along-lambda-area in eu-west-2 with Node.js 24, use the console-created default execution role, and deploy a handler that calculates an area.
tasks.whyItMatters: A Lambda handler receives the event object when invoked. The console can create a default execution role with basic CloudWatch Logs permissions for this simple function.

consoleSteps.title: Choose the practice Region
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The console Region selector shows Europe (London).
consoleSteps.warning: Lambda functions and CloudWatch log groups in this Follow Along are regional. Do not use a different Region.

consoleSteps.title: Open Lambda
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Functions page opens.

consoleSteps.title: Start function creation
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The basic function settings are visible.

consoleSteps.title: Set the function name
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The function name is follow-along-lambda-area.
consoleSteps.warning: Use this exact fixed name for the test, log review, verification, and manual cleanup.

consoleSteps.title: Select the runtime
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The selected runtime is Node.js 24.x.

consoleSteps.title: Keep the default architecture
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The architecture remains x86_64.

consoleSteps.title: Use the default execution role
consoleSteps.instruction: Keep the default execution-role option selected.

instructions.text: Keep the default execution-role option selected.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: Lambda will create a default execution role with basic logging permissions.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not create, edit, or attach an IAM policy in this Follow Along.

consoleSteps.title: Create the function
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The page for follow-along-lambda-area opens.

cliSteps.explanation: Use this read-only CLI check after creating the function with the console path.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes the function configuration, including the Node.js runtime and execution-role ARN.
cliSteps.warning: The AWS CLI create-function operation requires both a deployment package and an execution role. This beginner path creates the function in the console so Lambda can create the default execution role.

verification.title: Confirm the function configuration
verification.instruction: On the function page, review the function name and Runtime settings.
verification.expectedResult: The page shows follow-along-lambda-area and Node.js 24.x.

tasks.title: Replace and Deploy the Function Code
tasks.goal: Replace the starter code in index.mjs with a handler that calculates the area from length and width, then deploy the change.
tasks.whyItMatters: The handler is Lambda's entry point. This harmless handler reads a JSON event, writes a simple log message, and returns the calculated area.

consoleSteps.title: Open the code editor
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The Node.js starter code is visible.

consoleSteps.title: Replace the starter code
consoleSteps.instruction: Replace the file contents with `export const handler = async (event) => { const area = event.length * event.width; console.log(`The area is ${area}`); return JSON.stringify({ area }); };`.

instructions.text: Replace the file contents with `export const handler = async (event) => { const area = event.length * event.width; console.log(`The area is ${area}`); return JSON.stringify({ area }); };`.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The file exports handler and calculates an area from event.length and event.width.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not rename handler. Do not include secrets, credentials, or personal data in the code.

consoleSteps.title: Deploy the code
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The console reports that the function code was updated.
consoleSteps.warning: Editing code does not update the function until Deploy succeeds.

cliSteps.explanation: Use this read-only CLI check to confirm that the named function remains available after the console deployment.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response identifies follow-along-lambda-area in eu-west-2.
cliSteps.warning: This command does not show the editor contents. Use the console deployment confirmation to verify the code update.

verification.title: Confirm the handler is ready
verification.instruction: Review index.mjs and the deployment confirmation in the Lambda console.
verification.expectedResult: The file exports handler and the deployment completed successfully.

tasks.title: Invoke the Function with a Test Event
tasks.feature: Lambda test event and synchronous invocation
tasks.goal: Create the harmless area-test event containing length 6 and width 7, then invoke the function and confirm that the returned area is 42.
tasks.whyItMatters: A saved JSON event demonstrates how Lambda passes event data to the handler and gives you a repeatable test input.

consoleSteps.title: Create a test event
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The test-event editor opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Use only the fixed sample data in this Follow Along. Do not enter passwords, access keys, tokens, or personal information.

consoleSteps.title: Name the test event
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The event name is area-test.

consoleSteps.title: Enter the test JSON
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The event contains the two integer values 6 and 7.

consoleSteps.title: Save the test event
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The saved test event is named area-test.

consoleSteps.title: Run the test event
consoleSteps.instruction: Choose the run icon for area-test.

instructions.text: Choose the run icon for area-test.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The OUTPUT tab displays the invocation result.
consoleSteps.warning: If the test does not succeed, review the deployed handler code before continuing.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda invoke --function-name follow-along-lambda-area --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --payload '{"length":6,"width":7}' lambda-response.json --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Use this as the CLI alternative to invoke the already deployed function. The response body is written to the local file lambda-response.json.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The command response reports a successful invocation status, and lambda-response.json contains the function response.
cliSteps.warning: This command invokes the function and creates a local response file. It does not create an AWS resource. Use the fixed sample data only.

verification.title: Confirm the area result
verification.instruction: In the OUTPUT tab, inspect the result for area-test.
verification.expectedResult: The status is Succeeded and the response contains area 42.

tasks.title: Inspect the Invocation Log
tasks.goal: Open the Lambda invocation output and CloudWatch Logs evidence for the successful area-test invocation.
tasks.whyItMatters: Logs provide execution evidence and help connect a function invocation to its diagnostic output.

consoleSteps.title: Review invocation output
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The test response and function logs are visible.

consoleSteps.title: Find the custom log message
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The output includes the calculated-area log message.

consoleSteps.title: Open CloudWatch Logs
consoleSteps.expectedResult: CloudWatch opens the function log group.
consoleSteps.warning: Log delivery can take a short time after an invocation. Refresh only if the expected log evidence is not yet visible.

consoleSteps.title: Open the latest log stream
consoleSteps.instruction: Open the most recent log stream.

instructions.text: Open the most recent log stream.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The stream displays records for a recent invocation.

consoleSteps.title: Confirm the invocation records
consoleSteps.instruction: Find the START, END, and REPORT records.

instructions.text: Find the START, END, and REPORT records.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The log stream contains Lambda invocation records for the function.

cliSteps.command: aws lambda invoke --function-name follow-along-lambda-area --cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out --payload '{"length":6,"width":7}' lambda-log-response.json --log-type Tail --region eu-west-2
cliSteps.explanation: Use this optional CLI invocation to return up to 4 KB of base64-encoded invocation logs in the command response.
cliSteps.expectedResult: The response includes StatusCode and may include LogResult containing base64-encoded tail logs.
cliSteps.warning: This command performs another invocation and writes a local file named lambda-log-response.json. Do not decode or transform the output with chained commands in this Follow Along.

verification.title: Confirm the logging evidence
verification.instruction: Inspect the newest CloudWatch log stream for follow-along-lambda-area.
verification.expectedResult: The stream contains The area is 42 and Lambda invocation records.

warnings.cost: Lambda usage and CloudWatch Logs storage can create charges outside applicable free-tier allowances. Delete the exact practice function and log group when finished.
warnings.safety: All cleanup is manual. Confirm the exact resource name and eu-west-2 Region before deletion. Do not delete shared, unfamiliar, or service-linked IAM roles.
warnings.credentials: Do not create, paste, display, or store passwords, access keys, secret keys, tokens, or personal data in this Follow Along. The practice IAM user is intentionally created without credentials.
warnings.region: Create, invoke, inspect, and delete the Lambda function and its CloudWatch log group in Europe (London), eu-west-2. IAM users and IAM roles are global resources.

findings.message: The requested IAM user is created without console credentials and without permissions because this Follow Along must not create credentials or propose an IAM policy. The learner therefore continues the Lambda work using their existing authorized account session.

The console workflow is the creation path for the Lambda function because the AWS CLI create-function operation requires a deployment package and an execution role. This Follow Along does not create a separate execution role or provide a policy document.

The exact console wording and placement for test-event controls can vary as the Lambda console evolves. The AWS documentation describes the TEST EVENTS section and Create test event workflow; use the equivalent visible control if the layout differs.
